title: Ahrefs Pricing 2026: Plans, Credits, and Add-On Costs
summary: Ahrefs pricing starts at $129 monthly for the Lite plan, reaching $249 for Standard and $449 for Advanced, while Enterprise pricing isn't listed.
body_markdown:
## Automating Ahrefs reporting with Activepieces


Activepieces can't make the plan you chose any bigger, but it does not depend on a vendor's release schedule either.


If the connector you need is missing, you can generate the integration with AI and add it privately to your own instance, with no ticket in a queue. 746 integrations are counted straight from the open-source monorepo, and roughly 60% were contributed by the community.


Activepieces lets you set a trigger and chain steps that move data between apps without anyone writing code, and it runs unlimited flows on every plan, including the free one, so the number of reports you automate is never what you pay for.


### Ahrefs reports you can automate


Open the tool, copy the numbers, paste them into a spreadsheet, screenshot a chart for the client: that is the Monday-morning export most Ahrefs users know.


A workflow does that on a timer. A schedule trigger fires, an Ahrefs step fetches the data, and the results go to a Google Sheet, a Slack alert when something moves, and a client report.


That label is the part to take from it.


The Ahrefs step only works if your plan includes API access; everything on either side of it is ordinary plumbing. Whether you can use it at all, and how much you can pull, is decided by the plan you already hold.


Check that before you build anything. A workflow that depends on an API your plan doesn't include is a pretty diagram that returns nothing.


### What it does not change


**Automation doesn't lower the bill** . Your seats, usage limits and add-ons stay exactly where they were, and a workflow that pulls data every day draws on the same allowance you would use by hand.


If anything, an unattended schedule can reach your ceiling sooner than a person who only checks when they remember.


So treat Activepieces as a way to stop paying in staff hours for work a timer can do. It doesn't get you out of choosing the plan whose first limit you can live with. That choice comes first, and the workflow is built inside it.
